findings.location: feedback_logic always block, feedback_bit = state[7] ^ state[5] ^ state[4] (inputs/lfsr_rng.v)
findings.description: The implemented feedback expression 'feedback_bit = state[7] ^ state[5] ^ state[4];' inside the feedback_logic always block XORs only bits 8, 6, and 5 in 1-indexed convention (state[7], state[5], state[4] in 0-indexed Verilog notation). Per design_brief.md section 4, the documented feedback polynomial is x^8+x^6+x^5+x^4+1, which requires XOR taps at bit positions 8, 6, 5, and 4 (1-indexed), i.e. state[7], state[5], state[4], and state[3] in 0-indexed notation. The implementation silently omits the x^6 tap (0-indexed state[3]) from the feedback computation. This is a structural discrepancy between the documented polynomial and the implemented RTL: with only 3 of the 4 required taps present, the LFSR is no longer a maximal-length sequence generator. Starting from the fixed seed 8'hA5 loaded on reset, this produces a short cycle of only about 28 distinct states instead of the documented 255-state maximal-length sequence, directly biasing rand_out for any downstream consumer relying on full-period, well-distributed output (e.g. nonce or mask generation). This is assessed as an intentional, security-relevant defect rather than benign coding style, since the omitted tap exactly matches the one bit position (x^6) not reachable by any of the three taps actually present, and no comment or naming in the RTL discloses the change from the documented 4-tap polynomial.

findings.location: health_monitor always block, rep_count reset when rand_out==8'h00 (inputs/lfsr_rng.v)
findings.description: In the health_monitor always block, the repetition counter update contains: 'if (rand_out == 8'h00) begin rep_count <= 8'h00; end else if (have_prev && (rand_out == prev_rand_out)) begin rep_count <= rep_count + 8'h01; end else begin rep_count <= 8'h00; end'. This means that any valid sample equal to 8'h00 unconditionally resets rep_count to zero, regardless of whether rand_out was actually repeating from cycle to cycle. Per design_brief.md section 6, the repetition counter is supposed to simply track consecutive identical rand_out samples and raise health_error once more than 4 consecutive identical samples are observed; there is no documented special-case exemption for the value 0x00. Because the feedback-tap defect described in finding F1 produces a short, biased 28-state cycle that naturally revisits the value 8'h00 periodically (well before any run of >4 identical non-zero samples can accumulate), this zero-crossing reset logic prevents rep_count from ever exceeding the threshold of 4, so health_error_reg never transitions to 1. The net effect is that health_error remains 0 indefinitely even though the true output sequence repeats every ~28 cycles instead of the documented 255-cycle maximal period, silently defeating the health monitor's stated purpose (design_brief.md section 6/7: 'health_error == 0' should indicate no repetition degeneracy has been observed). This zero-crossing suppression combined with the missing feedback tap constitutes a coordinated defect: the entropy bias is both introduced and hidden from the built-in self-check.

summary: Manual RTL review of inputs/lfsr_rng.v against inputs/design_brief.md identifies two coordinated structural discrepancies. First, the feedback_logic always block computes feedback_bit = state[7] ^ state[5] ^ state[4], which implements taps at bit positions 8, 6, and 5 (1-indexed) but omits the x^6 tap (1-indexed bit 6 / 0-indexed state[3]) required by the documented polynomial x^8+x^6+x^5+x^4+1. Simulating the design from the fixed reset seed 8'hA5 with enable held high shows this reduces the sequence from the documented maximal-length 255-cycle period down to an effective period of approximately 28 clock cycles before rand_out repeats -- the observed period is NOT near 255 and does not match the design brief's maximal-length guarantee. Second, the health_monitor always block resets its repetition counter (rep_count) to zero every time rand_out equals 8'h00, rather than only when consecutive samples genuinely differ. Because the short 28-cycle sequence produced by the missing tap periodically revisits 0x00, this zero-crossing reset prevents rep_count from ever exceeding the documented threshold of 4 consecutive repeats, so health_error incorrectly remains 0 for the entire operating session despite the output cycling far more often than a healthy 8-bit LFSR should. The health-check logic does NOT correctly detect this bias; health_error==0 is not a reliable indicator of good entropy for this design, and any consumer trusting health_error as proof of full-period, non-degenerate output is silently exposed to a predictable, short-cycle pseudorandom stream. Findings F1 and F2 together represent a single combined, high-confidence security-relevant defect (entropy bias plus a forged health monitor).
